samples.summary: The CLI confirmation gate's route wiring (AuthModule.configure) has no test
samples.evidence: `CliLoginConfirmMiddleware` is the entire anti-CSRF gate for `?mode=cli` — `GitHubAuthGuard` only mints CLI state when `req.__cliConfirmed` is set, and only this middleware sets it. `cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts` tests the middleware in isolation (constructed directly, `middleware.use(req,res,next)`), and `github-auth.guard.spec.ts` tests the guard with `__cliConfirmed` injected by hand. Nothing asserts that the middleware is applied to `{ path: 'auth/github', method: GET }`, nor that it is resolvable by Nest (it is not listed in the module's `providers`). If the wiring is wrong or dropped, every spec in this diff stays green while every real CLI login silently degrades to a browser login (guard's `else` branch) — exactly the wiring-gap argument the authors themselves make in `github.strategy.spec.ts`. Searched: grep for `AuthModule|CliLoginConfirmMiddleware|configure(` across packages/backend/src (only auth.module.ts + the isolated middleware spec), and globbed packages/backend/src/auth/*.spec.ts — there is no auth.module.spec.ts or Nest `Test.createTestingModule` e2e for this route.

samples.summary: The CLI branch's invalid/expired-state 400 is now the fallthrough for any non-`web.` state and is untested
samples.evidence: The diff deleted the only test that exercised a non-CLI state (`falls back to web flow when state token is not CLI`) and replaced it with web-flow tests. After the change, any `state` that is a string but does not start with `web.` and does not resolve in `CliAuthStore` reaches `throw new BadRequestException('CLI login state expired or invalid...')` (auth.controller.ts:188), and `state.mode !== 'cli'` hits it too. No spec asserts this: grep for `expired or invalid`, `Invalid CLI port`, `BadRequestException` across packages/backend/src/auth matches only auth.controller.ts, never a spec. The `port < 1024 || port > 65535` guard at line 170 is likewise untested (`CliAuthStore.createState` accepts any port, so it is reachable).
searchedFor: grep 'expired or invalid|Invalid CLI port|BadRequestException' in packages/backend/src/auth

samples.summary: `omits state when the CLI sent no nonce` asserts too weakly — it passes on unrelated regressions
samples.evidence: The only assertion is `expect(url).not.toContain('state=')` on `res.redirect`'s first call. It never checks that the redirect is the loopback URL at all. If the CLI branch regressed to `res.redirect(this.loginErrorUrl('oauth_state'))` (`http://localhost:5173/login?error=oauth_state` — no literal `state=` substring) or to any other non-loopback URL, the test still passes. Its sibling at line 206 pins the loopback shape with a regex; this one should too (e.g. `expect(url).toMatch(/^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:9876\/callback\?code=[^&]+$/)`).

samples.summary: Single-use clearing of the OAuth state cookie is only asserted on the success path
samples.evidence: `res.clearCookie(cookieName, ...)` is deliberately issued before the match check (auth.controller.ts:158) so a failed callback also spends the cookie. Only `signs in when the state matches the cookie` (line 299) asserts `clearCookie`. The three refusal tests (lines 315, 328, 343) assert only `redirect` + `cookie not called`, so moving the `clearCookie` after the `if (!webOAuthStateMatches(...)) return` — leaving a mismatched-state cookie replayable — would keep the suite green.

samples.summary: Confirm-secret freshness and non-string `?confirm=` are untested in the middleware spec
samples.evidence: `cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts` never asserts that two unconfirmed requests get different secrets, so a regression to a constant secret (`res.cookie(name, 'x', …)`) — which would let an attacker mint a matching `?confirm=` — passes every existing case. It also never covers `?confirm=a&confirm=b` (an array), the case the controller spec explicitly pins for `state` at line 359; the `typeof confirm === 'string'` guard that handles it is therefore unexercised.
searchedFor: grep for randomBytes/secret assertions in the spec

samples.summary: The new `isCellTable` branch in `sheets import` is only tested at the helper level, not at the command
samples.evidence: `csv-parse.test.ts` covers `isCellTable` and `buildCellMapFromTable` as pure functions, but nothing drives `sheets import` end-to-end over an exported `ref,value,formula` CSV. Grep for `sheets-import` / `buildCellMapFromTable` across packages/cli shows the only test file is `test/csv-parse.test.ts`; there is no `test/sheets-import.test.ts` (compare `test/sheets-export.test.ts`, added in this diff). Swapping the branch arms, or passing `rows` instead of the table to the wrong builder, would not be caught.

`.replace(/\/+$/, '')` on FRONTEND_URL is new logic, but the spec's ConfigService always returns `http://localhost:5173` (auth.controller.spec.ts:34), so the strip is never exercised; a `FRONTEND_URL` of `http://x/` (producing `http://x//login?...`) or an unset value would go unnoticed.

finding.summary: The CLI confirmation gate's route wiring (AuthModule.configure) has no test
finding.evidence: `CliLoginConfirmMiddleware` is the entire anti-CSRF gate for `?mode=cli` — `GitHubAuthGuard` only mints CLI state when `req.__cliConfirmed` is set, and only this middleware sets it. `cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts` tests the middleware in isolation (constructed directly, `middleware.use(req,res,next)`), and `github-auth.guard.spec.ts` tests the guard with `__cliConfirmed` injected by hand. Nothing asserts that the middleware is applied to `{ path: 'auth/github', method: GET }`, nor that it is resolvable by Nest (it is not listed in the module's `providers`). If the wiring is wrong or dropped, every spec in this diff stays green while every real CLI login silently degrades to a browser login (guard's `else` branch) — exactly the wiring-gap argument the authors themselves make in `github.strategy.spec.ts`. Searched: grep for `AuthModule|CliLoginConfirmMiddleware|configure(` across packages/backend/src (only auth.module.ts + the isolated middleware spec), and globbed packages/backend/src/auth/*.spec.ts — there is no auth.module.spec.ts or Nest `Test.createTestingModule` e2e for this route.

verdict.reason: The claim holds. `auth.module.ts:39-50` binds `CliLoginConfirmMiddleware` to `GET auth/github` via `configure()`, and that binding is the only thing that activates the anti-CSRF gate (the guard mints CLI state only when `req.__cliConfirmed` is set, and only this middleware sets it). No test anywhere exercises the binding: repo-wide grep for `forRoutes|NestModule|MiddlewareConsumer` matches only `auth.module.ts`; grep for `AuthModule` matches only module sources and docs, never a spec; no `Test.createTestingModule`/supertest test hits `/auth/github` (the only occurrence under packages/backend/test is a `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` env string in helpers/integration-helpers.ts:94); `cli-login-confirm.middleware.spec.ts` constructs the middleware directly (line 16/32) with no Nest container; guard and strategy specs never touch module wiring; and there is no metadata-reflection assertion (`Reflect.getMetadata`) anywhere. Widened search into packages/cli and packages/frontend found only client-side URL assertions. Deleting `configure()` would leave every spec in the change green while all CLI logins silently degrade to browser logins — a security-relevant behavior with zero meaningful coverage, which is a major missing-test gap under this lens.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (2) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason: The finding contains no file, no test, and no test-adequacy claim; its text is verbatim the review harness's own infrastructure failure message. `poolExhaustedError()` at scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-637 constructs exactly the string "<label>: every credential in the pool (N) was retired — nothing left to fail over to", and docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-lessons.md:279 documents this same failure mode (a lens emitting findings with no verdict whose summary read "every credential in the pool ..."). So the "finding" is an artifact of the reviewing agent draining its credential pool, not a defect present in this repository. Reading it as charitably as possible — that the drained-pool behavior lacks coverage — is also false: scripts/agent/ask.test.mjs:295-308 asserts the error's message shape, kind ("pool-exhausted"), retryable=false and that no slot-specific text leaks; :310-326 asserts askStructured rejects on a pre-drained pool before opening a session; :328-349 asserts failoverStep hands back {next:"b"} while a credential remains, a pool-exhausted error on the last slot, and passes a non-credential error (error_max_turns) through untouched with retiredCount()===0; :351-359 asserts an all-bad pool drains once per slot and stops. Those assert real return values and state, not mock invocations, so they fail if the logic breaks. Nothing vacuous, missing, or over-mocked is identified by the finding.
